problem.h: You need a break, but scrolling isn’t one
p: At the end of a long day it’s easy to reach for the phone, and an hour later you feel more frazzled than when you started.
Proper rest is harder to find. A holiday is months away, and the to-do list is right there.

approach.h: Go somewhere else for a while
p: Each page is a little place to escape to: a cabin in the Highlands, a canal boat at dawn, an attic above the rooftops of Paris. In every one, there’s a cup waiting for you.
Pick a place that suits your mood: a simpler scene to unwind, or a fuller one when you want to get lost in the detail. Make the walls any colour you like. Add rain, or sunshine. Leave the kettle on.

offer.p: Detailed, calming line art for grown-ups, printed one picture to a page.
features: Cabins, attics, reading nooks and window seats, each with its own cup of something warm.
A mix of easier and fuller scenes, so there’s one for every kind of evening.
Every picture has its own page, so you can use pens as well as pencils.

note: I wanted colouring to feel like a tiny holiday, the kind you can take at the kitchen table with a cup of tea. Every scene has a cup in it somewhere, as a little invitation to sit down.
There’s no right way to colour them. Make the walls pink if you like.

faq: Can I use pens or markers?
Yes. Each picture is printed on its own page, so ink won’t spoil another design. If you use markers, slip a spare sheet of paper behind the page you’re colouring.
Yes. There’s a mix of simpler scenes and fuller, more detailed ones, so you can choose whatever suits your mood and confidence.
Is it for adults or children?
It’s designed for adults, with fine detail. Older children who enjoy detailed colouring may like it too.
Colouring pencils give the softest results. Gel pens and fine liners work well for small details.
It’s a lovely gift for someone who needs a breather: a new parent, a busy friend, or anyone who loves cosy things.

close.h: Make a cup of something warm
close.p: And go somewhere else for a while.
